Potentially inappropriate opinion time!!

It grinds my gears that the teacher put "ze" before "they"

I think adding countless new pronouns makes people less likely to actually use and respect them. Even as someone who isn't cisgender, I find it difficult to keep track of all of the different pronouns and how to say them. I would never tell anyone else not to use a particular pronoun, but as a genderqueer person, I would never ever use Xie or Bun or anything like that to refer to myself, and I've never met another genderqueer person in real life who uses those types of pronouns.

I've never heard from a non-binary person why they choose not to use "they", other than "I want to be different". Hey; it's totally their right to be different... but then people are going to treat you differently.

Honestly, if I encountered someone like that in real life, I would probably formulate my sentences so I wouldn't have to use any pronouns. Eventually, I would probably end up not hanging out with them as much as other friends... That's what happened with a couple female friends who are trans would get their thong in a knot about me saying stuff like "guys" when I was referring to "you people". I'm not a dude or a chick but I don't get pissed off when people say "hai guise" or refer to me using female pronouns (unless I'm in a LGBTQetc Safe Space, because they aren't following their own Safe Space policies)

I understand from a visceral level the feeling that gender =/= sex and that gender is not binary, but "they" is a term that's been used for the 1st person singular since the 14th century. Also, if it's hard enough for people from the Trans Community to get it, I don't expect someone who isn't even versed in Transgender 101 to understand. They aren't trying to be rude; but if you assume they are, they might act like an asshole just to spite you. It's not a "cissum" thing. It's a human thing.
